source.author: lucan
source.text: Ut matutinos spargens super aequora Phoebus Fregit aquis radios, et liber nubibus aether, Et posito Borea, pacemque tenentibus Austris, Servatum bello iacuit mare, movit ab omni Quisque suam statione ratem, paribusque lacertis Caesaris hinc puppes, hinc Graio remige classis Tollitur: impulsae tonsis tremuere carinae, Crebraque sublimes convellunt verbera puppes.
source.text_original: Ut matutinos spargens super aequora Phoebus / Fregit aquis radios, et liber nubibus aether, / Et posito Borea, pacemque tenentibus Austris, / Servatum bello iacuit mare, movit ab omni / Quisque suam statione ratem, paribusque lacertis / Caesaris hinc puppes, hinc Graio remige classis / Tollitur: impulsae tonsis tremuere carinae, / Crebraque sublimes convellunt verbera puppes.
source.text_english: As Phoebus, scattering his morning light over the seas, broke his beams upon the waters, and the sky was free of clouds and Boreas laid aside, while the South winds held peace, the sea, spared by war, lay still; each man moved his own vessel from every anchorage, and with equal arms Caesar’s ships were raised on this side, and on that the fleet with Greek rowers: the keels trembled, driven by the oars, and the lofty sterns were shaken by the frequent strokes.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: o si mihi sanguis, quantus erat, cum signiferum cratera minantem non leviore Pholum manus haec compescuit auro, primus in aeratis posuissem puppibus arma concussoque ratem gauderem tollere remo.
reuse.text_original: 'o si mihi sanguis, / quantus erat, cum signiferum cratera minantem / non leviore Pholum manus haec compescuit auro, / primus in aeratis posuissem puppibus arma / concussoque ratem gauderem tollere remo.
reuse.text_english: O if only I had had blood, such as it was when this hand checked Pholus, banner-bearer and threatening with the goblet, not with less gold, I would have been the first to place arms on bronze-clad ships and would have rejoiced to lift the vessel with the shaken oar.
